merger_description:
Colas Australia Group Pty Ltd (**Colas**), via its subsidiary Hutchison Quarries Toowoomba Pty Ltd, proposes to acquire the business known as Harlaxton Quarry or Quarry Products Harlaxton by acquiring:  

•    the operating quarry business and certain land and associated assets from Quarry Products Pty Ltd; and  

•    100% of the shares in Sanbeg Pty Ltd, which holds other land associated with the Harlaxton Quarry business  

(together, **Quarry Products Harlaxton**) (the **Acquisition**).  

Colas is an Australian construction materials and road services group. It operates quarrying business Hutchison Quarries near Warwick in the Southern Downs region of Queensland and is also a fully integrated bituminous materials supplier and applicator with its own bitumen and quarry resources, and road surfacing capabilities, operating through local subsidiaries across Australia.   

Hutchison Quarries supplies aggregates, road base and other crushed rock products.  

Quarry Products Harlaxton operates the Harlaxton Quarry, a basalt quarry located at Harlaxton / Toowoomba in Queensland supplying quarry materials used in rail, road, concrete, asphalt and civil construction applications, including rail ballast, road base and aggregates.   

Both Colas and Quarry Products Harlaxton supply aggregates, road base and oversize products.

events.title: Colas -Quarry Products Harlaxton - Phase 1 determination

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, information from third partes and publicly available
information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition would be unlikely to have
the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The merged entity would likely continue to face competition
from alternative suppliers of quarry materials in
Toowoomba/Warwick in the Southern Downs region of
Queensland.
• While a market participant suggested that the Acquisition could
enable the parties to foreclose rival suppliers of road
construction and road pavement services from accessing quarry
materials, the ACCC considers that the merged firm would be
unlikely to have the ability and incentive to do so. In particular,
rival suppliers would continue to have access to alternative
sources of quarry materials in the Toowoomba/Warwick region,
and Colas has limited downstream activities in the
Toowoomba/Warwick region.
